synthesis.description: Staff pass market information to traders and originators: a daily Western pre-scheduled firm electricity price report forwarded by an assistant, weather comparison spreadsheets, press articles on Enron's market role, analyst call notes, and regional supply and market analyses. Some rounds also ask recipients to review circulated data and pull out what is relevant to them, or offer a feed to a colleague who may want it.
steps: A report, article, analysis or set of call notes becomes available or is prepared.
The sender compiles or attaches the material, adding a short note on why it matters.
The material is forwarded to the trading or origination group or to named colleagues.
Recipients read it and, where asked, review it and pull the data relevant to their own work.
Ongoing analyses are assigned to a named person to keep compiling and updating.
synthesis.approach: Replace the manual daily forwarding of the published price report with a scheduled distribution that posts the report to a shared location and mails a subscribed list, and keep a simple subscription list so people can opt in to feeds instead of being asked one by one.
synthesis.rationale: Most rounds are the same report forwarded by hand each day, which a scheduled distribution handles well. A short checklist for the sender (which reports go to whom, where they are saved, who maintains each recurring analysis) keeps the remaining manual circulation consistent.
